mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -29.3% to -27.7%, indicates a nascent recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week surge in PARKS mobility from 14.0% to 28.3% reflects increased public comfort with outdoor activities, which will translate into higher overall out-of-home leisure and retail engagement over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in its weekly mean over the next two weeks following a week where PARKS mobility increased by more than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: The recent simultaneous increase in TRANSIT mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a shift away from home and towards public transport for movement, directly increasing foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT increasing and RESIDENTIAL decreasing in the preceding week.

mechanism_narrative: As workplace return policies become more prevalent, the slight improvement in WORKPLACES mobility combined with the recent dip in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a policy-driven shift back to physical offices, which will indirectly boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even if WORKPLACES mobility shows a positive trend and RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a negative trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals a broader increase in essential out-of-home errands, which typically precedes or accompanies a rise in discretionary retail and recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following two consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent, albeit slow, improvement in WORKPLACES mobility from -39.9% to -39.6% suggests a gradual return to office routines, which will incrementally increase demand for retail and recreation services near workplaces over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility continues to improve but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not show an upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recent increases in PARKS and TRANSIT mobility indicate a general resurgence of urban outdoor and public movement, creating more opportunities for spontaneous retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks when both PARKS and TRANSIT mobility show recent positive week-on-week changes.

mechanism_narrative: Despite minor recent upticks, the persistently high negative baseline for RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES, coupled with still elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicates that widespread caution and remote work habits will continue to suppress significant retail and recreation recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining highly negative and RESIDENTIAL remaining highly positive.
